segments: 3. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
and we despair of your goodness,
behold, we will enter inside,
and we will make known to all the zealous heroes who are with us.
And first, we will kill the Arab prisoners who are with us,
and then we will burn down your great mosque,
and then the churches and the rest of the buildings,
and then the possessions and household goods.
And then our wives and our sons and our daughters we will slaughter with our own hands,
and we will not leave you to satisfy your lust upon them.
And after this, not a single one of us will surrender himself to slaughter
without killing one or two in his place.'
When the Frank said these things,
the Sultan was astonished at his words.
And he had him escorted out and seated in one of the tents,
and he assembled the nobles and took counsel with them.
And they all replied together,
'Everything that this man said,
the Franks will do,
and even more than this.
And it is very good that he let them depart in peace.'
And the Sultan called those two and said to them,
'Your plea is accepted,
but it is not possible for all the people inside to depart for nothing.
The emirs who are with me want gold,
for they have toiled and lost much in the war.'
And the matter was resolved:
that every man should give ten dinars,
and every woman five,
and every boy or girl two dinars,
and they might depart with whatever they were able to carry.
And the Franks agreed to this,
and they weighed out thirty thousand dinars on behalf of the poor who had nothing to give;
and the rich weighed out for themselves and for other poor people;
and they all went out in peace.
Only the needy little ones who had no one to pay for them were led into captivity,
about five thousand souls.
Moreover, the Arab guards were bribed by many with a dinar each or more,
and they let them out.
And Muzaffar {OCR: Muzaffar?} al-Din ibn Zayn al-Din brought out a thousand souls of Syrians and Armenians for free, and said
that these were Edessenes,
the people of his flock.
And also the son of Shihab al-Din, the lord of Birah, brought out many others and said
that they were people of his country.
Now there was in Jerusalem a certain Greek queen,
who wore the habit of a nun,
and she lived in a monastery in Jerusalem.
She sent to Saladin that he should deal kindly with her,
and that no one should molest her.
And Saladin gave orders, and she departed
